::: {.lead}
Omar works in the office of Sunrise Company. Every month he writes a short
newsletter about the shop. This month he asks an AI assistant. In ten
seconds, the AI writes a nice text. It looks perfect. But three sentences
are wrong, and Omar does not see them. In this lesson you learn how these
tools write, where they fail, and when another tool is better.
:::

## Key terms

{{< glossary generative-ai prompt training-data hallucination knowledge-cutoff ai-bias search-engine >}}

## 3.1 How generative AI writes

Sara asks an AI assistant the same question two times. She gets two
different answers. Why?

An AI assistant learned from a huge amount of text: books, websites and
articles. This text is its **training data**. From it, the AI learned which
words often come together.

When you send a prompt, the AI writes **one likely word after another**
(@fig-how). It does not look up a fact in a list. It chooses a word that
often comes next. Often the likely word is also the true word. But not
always.

![How generative AI writes: one likely word after another.](images/genai-how.png){#fig-how width=100%}

::: {.callout-important title="Definition 3.1 — Generative AI"}
**Generative AI** makes new text or pictures from a prompt. It chooses
likely words. Likely is not the same as true.
:::

The AI does not always choose the most likely word. So the same prompt can
give a different answer each time. Some AI assistants also search the web
and show links to their sources. Then you can open a link and read the real
page.

::: {.callout-note title="Example 3.1 — The shop opens at …"}
The shop of Sunrise Company opens at 9 a.m. The AI does not read the shop's
records.

1. The AI writes "The shop opens at" and looks for the next word.
2. "8" is 45% likely, "9" is 40% likely, "10" is 15% likely.
3. The AI chooses "8". The sentence "The shop opens at 8 a.m." sounds right,
   but it is wrong.
:::

{{< sim file="sims/next-word.html" poster="sims/next-word.png" title="Next Word: how an AI writes a sentence" height="640" >}}

::: {.callout-note title="Lab task · Ask the same prompt twice"}
1. Open an AI assistant that the university allows, for example
   `copilot.microsoft.com`.
2. Type: *Write one sentence about the city of Amman.*
3. Start a new chat and type the same prompt again.
4. Copy both answers into a Word document.

*Your result:* two answers, and one sentence: are they the same or
different?
:::

## 3.2 Five weak spots of AI answers

Omar's newsletter says that the shop "won the Best Shop award". It did not.
AI answers sound sure, even when they are wrong. They have five weak spots
(@fig-spots).

![Five weak spots of AI answers.](images/ai-weak-spots.png){#fig-spots width=100%}

1. **Invented facts.** The AI can invent a book, a name, an award or a
   link. This is called a **hallucination**.
2. **Old information.** The AI learned from data up to a date: its
   **knowledge cutoff**. It may not know newer facts, prices or versions.
3. **Wrong numbers.** The AI can make mistakes in sums and percentages.
4. **Bias.** The AI can repeat unfair ideas from its data, for example
   that every nurse is a woman.
5. **Missing context.** The AI does not know your class, your job or your
   company, unless you tell it.

::: {.callout-important title="Definition 3.2 — Hallucination"}
A **hallucination** is an AI answer that sounds sure, but is invented or
wrong.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Example 3.2 — Twelve pens"}
Omar asks: "How much are 12 pens at 0.25 JD each?" The AI answers: "12 pens
cost 3.50 JD."

1. Omar checks with a calculator: 12 × 0.25 = 3.00 JD.
2. The AI answer is 0.50 JD too much.
3. The weak spot is a wrong number. For numbers, Omar uses a calculator or a
   spreadsheet.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Common mistake"}
"The AI gave a link, so it is true." Open the link. Sometimes the page does
not say the same thing, or the page does not exist.
:::

{{< sim file="sims/weak-spots.html" poster="sims/weak-spots.png" title="Weak Spots: what is wrong with this AI answer?" height="640" >}}

::: {.callout-note title="Lab task · Do these books exist?"}
1. Ask an AI assistant: *Give me 3 books about Microsoft Excel, with the
   author and the year.*
2. Search for each title in a search engine, for example `bing.com`.
3. For each book, write: found or not found.

*Your result:* a list of three books, each with "found" or "not found".
:::

## 3.3 AI, search engine or spreadsheet?

Mona has three jobs: find the last day to pay the university fees, add up
40 prices, and write a polite reminder e-mail. One tool is not best for all
three jobs (@fig-tools).

![Choose the right tool, then check.](images/tool-choice.png){#fig-tools width=100%}

| Tool | Best for | Example |
|---|---|---|
| AI assistant | drafts, summaries, ideas, translations | a polite reminder e-mail |
| search engine (Bing, Google) | today's facts, dates, rules, prices | the last day to pay fees, on the university website |
| spreadsheet (Excel) | exact sums, averages, lists of numbers | the total of 40 prices |

: Three tools and their best jobs. {#tbl-tools}

A **search engine** finds web pages. You open the page and read the real
source, for example the university website. When you use AI, follow five
steps: **ask, read, check, edit, use**. You are responsible for the text
that you use.

::: {.callout-note title="Example 3.3 — Mona's three jobs"}
1. The last day to pay the fees: a search engine, then the official
   university website. AI may know only an old date.
2. The total of 40 prices: a spreadsheet with SUM. It adds exactly.
3. The reminder e-mail: an AI assistant writes a draft. Mona reads it,
   checks the date in it, and changes it into her own words.
:::

{{< sim file="sims/right-tool.html" poster="sims/right-tool.png" title="Right Tool: AI, search or spreadsheet?" height="600" >}}

::: {.callout-note title="Lab task · AI or the website?"}
1. Ask an AI assistant: *What are the opening hours of the library of
   Al-Israa University?*
2. Open the university website and find the real opening hours.
3. Compare the two answers.

*Your result:* the two answers, and one sentence: which one do you trust,
and why?
:::

## Case study: Omar's newsletter

Omar asks an AI assistant for the October newsletter of Sunrise Company.
Then he checks every sentence against the company records.

| Company records, October 2026 | |
|---|---|
| Sales | September 3 500 JD, October 4 200 JD |
| New product | green tea cups |
| New staff | Lina and Sami |
| Shop hours | 9 a.m. to 6 p.m., Saturday to Thursday; closed on Friday |
| Awards | none |

: The facts that Omar checks against. {#tbl-records}

The AI draft has six sentences. Three are wrong: "a rise of 1 200 JD"
(4 200 − 3 500 = 700 JD), "won the Best Shop in Amman award in 2025"
(invented), and "open every day" (closed on Friday).

{{< sim file="sims/newsletter.html" poster="sims/newsletter.png" title="Newsletter Check" kind="game" height="660" >}}

::: {.callout-note title="Lab task · Check the newsletter"}
Play **Newsletter Check** (above). Mark each sentence OK or Fix, choose the
right fixes, and publish.

*Your result:* your stars, and the three mistakes in your own words.
:::

## Further reading

Evans, Martin and Poatsy, *Technology in Action*, 18th ed., the chapter on
artificial intelligence. UNESCO, *Guidance for Generative AI in Education
and Research*, 2023.

## Exercises

1. What is training data?
2. Why can the same prompt give two different answers?
3. Write the five weak spots of AI answers.
4. What is a hallucination? Give one example.
5. An AI says: "The newest version of the app is from 2021." Which weak spot
   can this be?
6. An AI says: "15% of 200 is 35." Is it right? Which weak spot is it?
7. Which tool do you use for each job: today's price of gold, a summary of
   an article, the average of 25 marks?
8. Write the five steps when you use AI.

## Answers to the exercises

::: {.answers}
1. The huge amount of text and other data that an AI learned from.
2. The AI chooses likely words, and not always the most likely one.
3. Invented facts, old information, wrong numbers, bias, missing context.
4. An answer that sounds sure but is invented or wrong; for example, a book that does not exist.
5. Old information (its knowledge cutoff).
6. No: 15% of 200 is 30. A wrong number.
7. A search engine; an AI assistant; a spreadsheet.
8. Ask, read, check, edit, use.
:::
